events.title: First Human Flight in a Balloon
events.description: Jean-François Pilâtre de Rozier rose into the air in a Montgolfier brothers hot-air balloon. The balloon was tethered, and the flight was the first time a human left the ground in any aircraft.
events.significance: It opened the age of aviation and showed that people could travel above the earth.

events.title: Napoleon Begins His Exile on Saint Helena
events.description: Napoleon Bonaparte arrived on the remote South Atlantic island of Saint Helena. The British had sent him there after his defeat at Waterloo.
events.significance: This marked the final end of Napoleon's rule. He lived out his last years on the island, far from the European continent he had once dominated.

events.title: Mata Hari Is Executed
events.description: The Dutch exotic dancer Mata Hari was executed by firing squad at Vincennes, near Paris. She had been convicted of spying for Germany during the First World War.
events.significance: Her name became shorthand for the glamorous female spy, though historians still debate how strong the case against her was.

events.title: Graf Zeppelin Completes Its First Transatlantic Flight
events.description: The German airship Graf Zeppelin landed at Lakehurst, New Jersey, finishing its first flight across the Atlantic Ocean.
events.significance: The voyage showed that airships could carry passengers over long distances, and it began a short golden age of luxury air travel.
